about.tagline: The open-source, self-hosted Platform-as-a-Service (PaaS) for Docker.

ports.declareHint: Declares a port the container listens on. Scheme is how a Gateway route reaches it (use https for TLS-only backends). Applies on the next deploy.
ports.noBindings: No host bindings. Requests require admin approval before they publish.
ports.schemeHint: Application protocol the container speaks on this port
ports.suggestHint: Host ports are shared per node — “Suggest” picks one that’s currently free.

settings.addCapsHint: Granted on top of Docker's default set, like {cmd}. Applied on the next deploy. Grant only what the image actually needs — each one widens what a compromise of this container reaches.
settings.alwaysOnRestricted: Always on under this workspace’s restricted security profile.
settings.buildCacheHint: Builds reuse cached layers. Invalidate when a cached layer has gone stale — the next build rebuilds every layer and repopulates the cache. Nothing is deleted.
settings.cmdProbeHint: Runs via the shell; non-zero exit = unhealthy.
settings.commandHint: Overrides the image's default command (CMD). Space-separated args; leave blank to use the image default.
settings.devicesAllowed: Exposed at the same path inside the container. Allowed:
settings.devicesNoBlock: . Raw block devices are never granted — they are the host's filesystem.
settings.dropCapsHint: Removed from Docker’s default set, like {cmd}. {all} drops every one, leaving only the capabilities granted to the app. Applied on the next deploy.
settings.gitopsLocked: Managed by GitOps — change it in the Git manifest. Edits here are overwritten on the next {link}.
settings.gpuFilterHint: Narrow to a vendor/model (e.g. {vendor}). Empty = any enabled GPU on the node.
settings.gpuHint: Whole GPU devices to attach. 0 = none. Counts against the plan’s GPU quota while running.
settings.hostMountsHint: Bind allow-listed host paths into this app. These grant host-level access — attach only what the app truly needs.
settings.httpProbeHint: Uses {curl} (or {wget}) inside the container — the image must include one.
settings.needsDeveloper: You need developer access to edit settings.
settings.noNewPrivilegesHint: Stops processes gaining privileges through setuid binaries, like {flag}.
settings.noRepoPipelineHint: This app builds directly. If you have added a {file} to the repository, re-sync to adopt it.
settings.pipelineBuildsHint: The steps in {path} decide how the image is built, so the build method and builder below no longer apply.
settings.pipelineBuildsTitle: This app builds through its repository's pipeline.
settings.pullPolicyHint: Whether a deploy pulls the image from the registry: {always} fetches the tag each deploy, {ifNotPresent} reuses a locally cached image, {never} requires it to be present already. Digest-pinned images are never re-pulled.
settings.readOnlyRootHint: The container can write only to its volumes. An image that writes elsewhere, such as {path}, needs a volume mounted there or it fails to start. One-off jobs keep a writable filesystem.
settings.reconcileHint: What the platform's reconciliation does when this app's container is gone from its node: {default} follows the server-wide setting, {ignore} stops watching it at all, {report} records the problem without touching it, and {redeploy} brings it back on the same node. A missing data volume always stops a redeploy — the data has to be restored first.
settings.repoPipelineHint: Deploys run {path} from the repository. Re-sync after editing it to pick the changes up now instead of at the next deploy.
settings.restartPolicyHint: When the container should be restarted by Docker. Applied on the next deploy.
settings.runAsUserHint: The account the container runs as, like {cmd} — {a}, {b} or a name from the image ({name}). Blank keeps the image’s own user. Attached volumes are chowned to it on the next deploy.
settings.runAsUserRestricted: This workspace runs under the restricted security profile: give a non-root numeric uid. A name can’t be used, because the image decides what it maps to.
settings.savedRepoHint: A saved repository supplies the clone URL and credentials.
settings.sourceHint: Where this application's image comes from.
settings.stackHint: Stack changes take effect on the next deploy.
settings.subtitle: Runtime settings applied on the next deploy.
settings.switchKept: Domains, environment variables, volumes and history are kept.
settings.switchPipelineRemoved: Its repository pipeline ({path}) will also be removed.
settings.switchToGitBody: The image and registry credential will be cleared, and the app needs a redeploy to run from the new source.
settings.switchToImageBody: The repository, branch and build settings will be cleared, and the app needs a redeploy to run from the new source.
settings.templateImageWarning: Changing the image here means it no longer matches the template, and a future template upgrade may overwrite it.
settings.waitHealthyHint: Deploys wait for the container to report healthy before going live.

canary.exclusiveLabel: Exclusive — matching requests go entirely to the canary, ignoring the weight
canary.ipWarning: This rule set routes on client IP. Unless the gateway has {setting} configured, the client address is whatever the caller claims — anyone could put themselves in the canary.
canary.manualHint: Hold the canary at a weight you choose instead of watching an automatic ramp, and send only the requests you pick — a header, a cookie, a query parameter, an IP — to the new release.
canary.manualModeHint: The weight stays where you put it, and match rules can steer who reaches the canary.
canary.previewHint: Resolves a request against the {saved} rules. Nothing is deployed and no traffic moves — save your changes first to preview them.
canary.priorityHint: Breaks ties when several exclusive backends match. One canary per app today, so this is reserved.
canary.rampHint: The platform raises the weight on a timer and promotes at 100%.
canary.readOnlyNotice: This canary keeps routing exactly as configured, but the licence has expired, so the rules are read-only. {link} to change them.
canary.rulesHint: A request reaches the canary only when {every} rule holds. With no rules, the weight alone decides.
canary.weightHintManual: the only thing that moves traffic

certificates.acmeIssueHint: Miabi solves an ACME DNS-01 challenge via your provider and stores the certificate here. This can take a minute.
certificates.importHint: Import a certificate + private key to terminate TLS with your own cert. One wildcard cert can back many routes.
certificates.keyHint: The key is validated against the certificate, encrypted at rest, and never shown again.

certificates.unusedHint: Not used by any route. The certificate can be safely deleted.
certificates.verifiedOnlyHint: Only verified domains with a connected DNS provider can be issued.

clusterDetail.removeNameFromThe: Remove {name} from the swarm? It becomes a standalone cluster of its own.
clusterDetail.theAgentIsRemoved:
The agent is removed from every cluster node. They keep running their tasks — Swarm schedules those itself — but Miabi loses its Docker connection to them.

Apps scheduled on those nodes will stop showing metrics, stats and a shell. The node records themselves are kept.

nodeDetail.removeContainerToremovecontainerThis: Remove container "{toRemoveContainer}"? This cannot be undone.
nodeDetail.removeNodeNameIts: Remove node "{name}"? Its agent tunnel is closed and the edge gateway (if any) is torn down.
nodeDetail.removeTheGomaGateway: Remove the Goma Gateway container from this node? Routing through it stops until you redeploy. ACME certs are preserved.
nodeDetail.swarmReschedulesThisNode:
Swarm reschedules this node's service tasks onto other nodes now, and places no new ones here. This is what makes the node safe to reboot.

Note: setting it back to Active does NOT move the tasks back. Swarm never rebalances on its own — they stay where they were rescheduled until a redeploy, a scale, or a drain of their new node moves them again.

organizationDetail.displayNameWillBe: "{display_name}" will be removed, and any location dedicated to it becomes administrator-only until you reassign it. Deleting is refused while it still holds workspaces or users.

organizations.displayNameWillBe: "{display_name}" will be removed and any cluster dedicated to it returns to shared. Deleting is refused while it still holds workspaces or users — move those first.
organizations.newUsersAndWorkspaces: New users and workspaces that name no organization will belong to "{display_name}". Existing ones do not move.{promoteWarning}
organizations.promoteWarning: {name} runs its own locations ({where}), so new users and workspaces that name no organization will deploy there and nowhere else.

planDetail.deletePlanNameAny: Delete plan "{name}"? Any workspaces using it will fall back to the default plan.

platformBackup.restore: Restore {what}? This is destructive. Put the platform in maintenance mode first. You also need the original MIABI_ENCRYPTION_KEY to decrypt restored secrets.

restoreWhat.database: the control-plane database (overwrites the running database in place)

platformBackup.schedulesAndCertificateIssuance: Schedules and certificate issuance resume. Do this only once DNS points at this host — otherwise certificate requests will be issued against an address that still resolves elsewhere.

routes.exploitProtectionHint: Rejects requests carrying common injection and traversal signatures at the gateway, before the backend sees them. Off by default — a strict backend may already reject them, and a noisy filter can block legitimate traffic.
routes.generatedHint: Auto-generated for external access; managed from the app's External Access
routes.generatedRouteHint: This route is created and reconciled automatically for the application's external access. Enable, disable, or remove it from the app's {card} card — it can't be edited or deleted here.
routes.maintenanceHint: The gateway answers this route itself; the backend is never reached
routes.maintenanceOffHint: Requests reach the app as usual. Parking answers at the gateway instead, so a deploy or a migration stays invisible to visitors.
routes.maintenanceOnHint: Every request gets {status} from the gateway. The app is still running and never sees the traffic.
routes.managedHint: Managed from the app's External Access
routes.messageIsJson: Your message parses as JSON, so it is returned as written.
routes.messageNotJson: Not valid JSON, so the gateway wraps it in its own envelope.
routes.messageXmlHint: XML is always wrapped and escaped — a hand-written XML message is not passed through.
routes.middlewaresHint: Attach Goma middlewares (auth, rate-limit, headers…) to this route without editing it.
routes.middlewaresOnGeneratedHint: Allowed on auto-generated routes, so you can secure external access in place.
routes.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (e.g. my-api).
routes.noDomainsHint: No domains registered. Enter a host manually, {link} to pick from a list, or leave blank to match all hosts.
routes.noHostsHint: No hosts — this route will match all hosts (catch-all).
routes.noMiddlewaresHint: No middlewares defined in this workspace yet. {link} to attach it here.
routes.noPublicAddressHint: No public address is set for the node serving this route. Set its {field} on the node's page so Miabi can show the record to create.
routes.overridesHint: {name} and {backends} are managed by Miabi; everything else (path, hosts, methods, middlewares, rewrite, cors, rateLimit, …) comes from here.
routes.previewTextHint: Browsers land here: the {header} header they send matches none of the structured formats.
routes.rootDomainHint: Leave a subdomain blank to serve the domain at its root. Routes: {host}
routes.saveOrderFirst: Save or discard the order change first
routes.subtitle: Goma Gateway routes for your applications.

runners.concurrencyHint: How many jobs this runner may run at once.
runners.emptyHint: Register a build machine so builds and pipelines run here instead of on your app nodes.
runners.labelsHint: A job runs on this runner only when its required labels are all present.
runners.noSharedRunners: No platform-shared runners are available yet.
runners.tokenHint: This is the only time it is shown. Run the runner on your build machine:

secretPicker.searchPlaceholder: Search secrets by name or description…

secrets.emptyHint: Store a secret once and reference it from many apps. Rotating it updates every consumer on next deploy.
secrets.generateValueLabel: Generate a value for this secret
secrets.managedHint: Auto-created and managed by a database; rotate or remove via that database
secrets.noMatches: No secrets match the current search and filter.
secrets.searchPlaceholder: Search secrets by name or description…
secrets.subtitle: Reference these from any app's env, e.g. {ref} Values are resolved at deploy time and never shown unless revealed.
secrets.valueHint: Stored verbatim — line breaks and trailing newlines are preserved.
secrets.valuePlaceholder:
the secret value

Multi-line values are stored exactly as entered, so a PEM certificate or private key can be pasted whole.

security.codesRemaining: No recovery codes remaining. | {n} recovery code remaining. | {n} recovery codes remaining.
security.enterCodeHint: Enter the 6-digit code it shows to confirm.
security.lowOnCodes: You're running low on recovery codes
security.manualKey: Can't scan? Enter this key manually: {key}
security.passwordSubtitle: Change the password you use to sign in to Miabi.
security.recoveryCodesHint: Each code works once if you lose access to your authenticator. They won't be shown again.
security.regenerateHint: Regenerate a fresh set so you don't get locked out.
security.scanHint: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app.
security.twoFactorHint: Add an extra layer of security to your account by requiring a time-based code from an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, 1Password, Authy…) in addition to your password.

shellTerminal.escGoesToTheShell: Esc goes to the shell · Shift+Tab to leave it

stacks.addAppHint: Add an application to group it under this stack.
stacks.displayNameHint: The label shown in the console. Leave blank to fall back to the stack's name.
stacks.emptyHint: Create a stack to group related applications and manage their containers together.
stacks.importHint: One application is created per image-based service (ports, env, command). Named volumes are provisioned and mounted, and apps resolve each other by service name within the stack. Published host ports become pending bindings an admin approves. Build-only services and bind mounts are skipped.
stacks.labelsHint: Compose labels apply when the application is next deployed.
stacks.nameHint: Permanent. The Docker project name ({project}), the stack's network and its GitOps identity all derive from it. To use a different name, create a new stack and move the apps across.
stacks.redeployHint: Configuration changed since this app was last deployed — redeploy to apply it
stacks.rollingRestart: Restart one app at a time
stacks.searchPlaceholder: Search stacks by name, description, or Docker name…
stacks.sharedEnvHint: Injected into every app in the stack on its next deploy. An app's own variable with the same key wins.

switcher.privilegedTitle: A privileged workspace: host mounts and host-port bindings are allowed without approval, and the restricted security profile does not apply.
switcher.systemTitle: The built-in platform workspace. It holds platform-managed resources and cannot be renamed or deleted.

verifyEmail.verificationLinksExpireAndCan: Verification links expire and can only be used once. Sign in to have a new one sent, or ask your platform administrator to verify the address for you.
verifyEmail.yourAddressIsConfirmedYou: Your address is confirmed. You can sign in now.

volumes.backupNeedsS3: Enable S3 in workspace backup settings first
volumes.backupNow: Back up this volume to S3
volumes.backupsDisabledHint: Volume backups are disabled — no S3 target is configured for this workspace. Enable one in {link}.
volumes.backupsHint: Compressed archives stored in the workspace S3 target.
volumes.deleteHint: Permanently removes the volume and all its data. This cannot be undone.
volumes.detachFirst: Detach it from every application first.
volumes.emptyHint: Create persistent storage to attach to your applications.
volumes.hostBindHint: Bind a path your operator has mounted at the same location on every node (e.g. a NAS at /mnt). No credentials stored in Miabi; a replicated cluster app can share it.
volumes.hostPathHint: Must be an absolute path under {root}. The operator is responsible for mounting the storage at this exact path on every node.
volumes.localHint: Lives on one node. Use for single-replica apps.
volumes.missingHint: The underlying Docker volume was not found
volumes.nasHint: Shared (RWX) storage on your NAS — a replicated cluster app can mount it across nodes.
volumes.noBackups: No backups yet. Configure S3 in workspace backup settings, then back up this volume.
volumes.noMounts: No applications mount this volume. It can be safely deleted.
volumes.restoreHint: Restore this backup into the volume
volumes.rwoHint: Node-local (RWO) storage — lives on one node
volumes.rwxHint: Shared (RWX) {driver} storage — usable by a replicated cluster app across nodes
volumes.sharedNotInPlan: Shared storage (NFS / CIFS-SMB) isn't included in this workspace's plan.
volumes.sizeHint: Declared capacity, recorded for quota accounting. Hard enforcement depends on the node's storage backend.

webhooks.emptyHint: Notify external services (CI, chat, automations) on deploy and container events.
webhooks.headersHint: {format}. Content-Type and the signature header are always set.
webhooks.secretHint: This is the only time it is shown. Use it to verify the {header} header (HMAC-SHA256 of the request body).
webhooks.subtitle: POST a signed JSON payload to your endpoints when app events fire.

wsSettings.bundlePassphraseHint: Seals a portable bundle's secrets and encrypts its dumps. Record it outside Miabi: it is the only thing that opens a bundle on another install — including one rebuilt after losing this one.
wsSettings.changingItUpdatesEveryUrl: Changing it updates every URL and the docker handle
wsSettings.dbPassphraseHint: Encrypts every database backup before it is stored. Without one, dumps are written to the bucket in plain text. Record it outside Miabi — a backup cannot be restored without it. Backups already taken stay readable as they are.
wsSettings.dedicatedNodesChip: Running on {org}'s own nodes in {location} — not shared with any other organization.
wsSettings.dedicatedNodesHint: {org} runs its own nodes. This workspace's apps, databases and volumes run there, and no workspace outside {org} can be placed on them — not even by a platform administrator. The location follows the organization rather than this workspace.
wsSettings.defaultLocationHint: Where new apps, databases, volumes and stacks run when their form names no location.
wsSettings.deleteHint: Permanently removes the workspace, repositories, and all associated resources. This action cannot be undone.
wsSettings.deleteWarning: This permanently removes {name} and {resources} — applications, databases, volumes and stacks. This cannot be undone.
wsSettings.displayNameHint: The free-text label shown across the UI.
wsSettings.enableS3BackupsForThis: Enable S3 backups for this workspace
wsSettings.handleHint: The unique handle in the workspace's URLs and its {docker} namespace. Lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. {warning}, and reserved names are not allowed.
wsSettings.inviteTokenHint: Share this token with the invitee — it is shown only once.
wsSettings.limitsAreShownForReference: Limits are shown for reference; enforcement is disabled platform-wide.
wsSettings.liveUsageHint: Actual consumption right now across the workspace's running app & database containers.
wsSettings.needAdminBackups: You need admin access to manage backup settings.
wsSettings.needAdminExport: You need admin access to export or restore this workspace.
wsSettings.needAdminSettings: You need admin access to edit workspace settings.
wsSettings.pathStyle: Force path-style URLs (required by MinIO and some S3-compatible stores)
wsSettings.probeNotDeletable: — written and read back, but not deletable
wsSettings.s3Hint: One bucket and credentials shared by database and volume backups. The secret is stored encrypted and never shown again.
wsSettings.securityDefaultHint: Containers run as the image default user
wsSettings.securityRestrictedHint: App and job containers run as a non-root platform UID
wsSettings.systemNameLocked: The built-in platform workspace cannot be renamed.
wsSettings.theSystemWorkspaceNameIs: The system workspace name is reserved and cannot be changed.
wsSettings.turnEncryptionOff: Turn encryption off — new backups will be stored unencrypted
